struck: The seller's one duty is a one-page form, before the contract.
use: Unless the sale is exempt, the seller fills in the state's disclosure form before the contract is signed. If the home is in an association, that includes a one-page HOA addendum.

pattern: \brules?\b[^.]{0,120}\bmust be (?:given|handed|provided|made available|made accessible) to (?:a |any )?(?:member|owner)s? who asks?\b
struck: Rules and regulations take effect when adopted, must be given to a member who asks, and stay enforceable only if recorded at the county.
use: Rules take effect when adopted. An association must give a member a copy on request unless they are posted in a common area or on its website.

struck: A member may inspect and copy the association's bylaws, articles, minutes and financial statements of the past three years.
use: An owner of a nonprofit association can inspect and copy its articles, bylaws, minutes of owners' meetings and three years of financial statements.

struck: A condo buyer is liable with the seller for the seller's unpaid assessments.
use: A condo buyer, other than a buyer at a foreclosure sale, owes the seller's unpaid assessments along with the seller.

struck: For a conventional loan on a condo, the lender checks that the budget puts at least 10 percent of dues income into reserves.
use: In Fannie Mae's full review of a condo building, the budget must put at least 10 percent of dues income into reserves.

struck: For applications from January 4, 2027, the reserve line rises to 15 percent.
use: Freddie Mac raises its test to 15 percent for loan applications from January 4, 2027.

struck: A building that a lender's review finds ineligible cannot get a standard conventional loan.
use: A loan on a unit there cannot be sold to Fannie Mae, so buyers need a different loan.
